title: Still probably not endorsed by British Royal family though lol 🙃 #the...
transcript: what if Prince George of England grew up to be the first openly gay heir to the British throne and was also into k!nk culture? that's the provocative premise of this new play with an equally provocative title and if your first thought was “wow that sounds like a really disrespectful thing to write a play about!” I would encourage you to see it before judging because the play tackles your concerns head on and ends up being this impressively thoughtful nuanced and poignant piece of drama that's very clear about what it is and isn't trying to explore there's seriously a lot to unpack with this play more than I could possibly do in this short video but one thing that kept coming up for me as I was processing it is that so much of it to me was about the clashing of opposing forces that are orbiting around this one person at the same time: archaic tradition vs. modern sensibilities privilege vs. marginalization and the large divide between superficial acceptance and true liberation even the format of the play is like this pretty traditional drama but then it's disrupted and reframed by more experimental elements: monologues that break the 4th wall that might appear extraneous at first but are actually essential to the point of the play but at the same time it's able to do all of that while also just being a very compelling narrative I really think this is one of the strongest plays of the season and you know it would be a really bold swing to put this up on Broadway but at the very least I do think it deserves another run in the meantime though it's running through July 27th
